name: Gutter Installation
title: Gutter Installation in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: New gutter installation across Dallas–Fort Worth. Correct sizing, slope, and downspout placement to move water away from your foundation.
heroSub: In expansive clay soil, where your roof water lands is a foundation question, not a landscaping one.
intro: North Texas sits on soil that swells when wet and shrinks when dry. Dumping several thousand gallons of roof runoff against the same six feet of foundation every season is one of the more expensive habits a house can have.

Good gutters are mostly about unglamorous decisions: enough capacity for the roof area feeding them, correct slope to the outlets, downspouts in the right places, and discharge far enough from the house to matter.

signs.d: Bare channels in beds or mulch mark where water is falling directly off the edge.

signs.t: Splashback staining on brick or siding
signs.d: A visible dirt line low on the wall.
Persistent wet spots after rain, right where you least want them.

signs.t: No gutters at all on some elevations
signs.d: Very common on North Texas homes, especially over back patios and side yards.

causes.d: Five-inch gutter on a large steep roof plane simply cannot carry the volume.
Capacity is limited by outlets as much as by trough size.
Standing water in the trough means debris settles and seams work harder.

causes.t: Discharge too close to the house
causes.d: A downspout that empties at the foundation has moved the problem eight feet, not solved it.

Assess existing slope, seams, and hanger spacing
Identify where downspouts should discharge
Check fascia condition before hanging anything on it
Look at grading and where water actually goes

process.d: Roof area, elevations, and drainage reviewed together.
Sizing, material, color, and downspout plan itemized.
Seamless runs formed to the length of each elevation.
Hung with correct slope and hanger spacing, outlets and downspouts placed to plan.
Flow verified, site cleaned.
Anything soft gets replaced before new gutters are hung on it, rather than after they pull loose.

options.d: The standard residential system across North Texas.
Higher capacity for large roof planes, steep pitches, or long runs.
Larger or additional downspouts where volume calls for it.
Moving water meaningfully away from the foundation.
Carrying discharge far enough from the slab to matter in clay soil.
Selected against your fascia, trim, and brick in daylight rather than from a chart.

benefits: Sized to the roof area actually feeding each run
Fascia checked before anything is hung on it
Downspouts placed for drainage, not just for appearance
Free written estimate with color options
localNote: Foundation movement is a defining feature of North Texas homeownership. Gutters will not solve a structural problem, but consistent, controlled roof drainage is one of the few genuinely preventative things a homeowner can do about soil moisture swings.

faqs.q: Do I need 5-inch or 6-inch gutters?
faqs.a: It depends on roof area, pitch, and run length. Larger, steeper roof planes shed water faster than a 5-inch trough can carry, and that is when overflow happens in heavy rain.

faqs.q: Can gutters be installed on a house that never had them?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Fascia condition needs checking first, and occasionally fascia repair is a prerequisite.

faqs.q: How far should downspouts discharge from the house?
faqs.a: Further than most are. Extensions and buried drainage both work; the right answer depends on your grade and lot.

name: Seamless Gutters
title: Seamless Gutters in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: Seamless aluminum gutters formed on site for DFW homes — fewer joints, fewer leak points, and a cleaner line along the roof edge.
heroSub: Every seam is a future leak. Seamless runs remove most of them.
intro: Sectional gutters join every ten feet or so, and each of those joints is a place sealant eventually fails. Seamless gutters are formed continuously to the length of the elevation, so joints exist only at corners and outlets.
The practical difference in this climate is longevity. Texas heat is hard on gutter sealant, and fewer seams means fewer places for it to matter.

signs.d: Staining or dripping at regular intervals along a run points at seam failure.
Older sectional systems commonly sag at the joints.
If you have caulked the same joint more than once, the system is telling you something.

causes.d: UV and thermal cycling break down joint sealant faster here than in milder climates.
Aluminum expands and contracts daily, working every joint.
Seams catch material and hold moisture against the sealant.

inspection: Assess existing runs, joints, and hanger condition
Measure each elevation for continuous forming
Check fascia for soundness
Confirm downspout locations and capacity

process.d: Each elevation measured for a continuous run.
Free, with color and profile options.
Runs formed to exact length so no mid-run joints are created.
Hung to slope, outlets fitted, flow verified.
The board the system hangs from inspected before anything is fabricated.
Flow verified through every run and outlet before we leave the site.

options.d: The common residential profile, available in 5-inch and 6-inch.
Selected against fascia, trim, and brick.
Sized to the trough and the roof area it serves.
For large or steep roof planes that outrun a standard trough in heavy rain.
Concealed hangers at correct spacing rather than visible spikes.
Replacing the joints that actually fail while keeping sound runs in place.

benefits: Joints limited to corners and outlets

Fewer maintenance points over the system's life
localNote: Long uninterrupted rooflines are common on North Texas ranch-style and newer suburban homes, which is exactly where seamless forming pays off most — a forty-foot run with no mid-span joints instead of four.

faqs.q: Are seamless gutters really seamless?
faqs.a: The runs are. Corners, end caps, and outlets are still joined — there is no way around that — but the long spans between them are continuous.

faqs.q: Can seamless gutters be repaired?
faqs.a: Yes. Sections can be replaced, and corners and outlets can be resealed or rebuilt.

heroSub: A gutter that overflows is doing the opposite of its job.
intro: Most gutter problems are small and mechanical: a hanger pulled loose, a seam that gave up, a downspout packed with debris, or a run that has lost its slope. None of those require replacing the whole system.
The reason to deal with them promptly is what overflow water does on the way down — rotting fascia, saturating soil at the foundation, and washing out beds.

localNote: Post-storm gutter damage is one of the most reliable indicators of hail in North Texas. If your gutters and downspouts are dented, the roof above them is worth a free inspection at the same time.

faqs.q: Can you repair gutters and inspect the roof in the same visit?
faqs.a: Yes, and it usually makes sense to. Gutter condition and roof condition are related more often than not.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing old gutters?
faqs.a: Frequently, yes. If the material is sound and the problem is slope, hangers, or seams, repair is the sensible answer.

name: Gutter Guards
title: Gutter Guards in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: Gutter guard options for DFW homes, with straight talk about what they do well and where they fall short.
heroSub: They reduce cleaning. They do not eliminate it. Anyone telling you otherwise is selling.
intro: Gutter guards keep leaves and larger debris out of the trough, which matters a lot if you have mature oaks or pines over the roofline. They are genuinely useful and they are routinely oversold.
What they do not do is make a gutter maintenance-free. Fine debris and shingle granules still get through most designs, and guards themselves need occasional attention.

localNote: Tree cover varies enormously across the Metroplex. Older neighborhoods in East Dallas, Richardson, and Arlington sit under mature canopy where guards earn their keep. Newer developments in Celina or Prosper often have young trees and much less need.

faqs.q: Will guards mean I never clean my gutters?
faqs.a: No. They reduce how often and how badly. Fine grit and granules still accumulate.

faqs.q: Can guards cause overflow?
faqs.a: Some designs can in very heavy rain, particularly in valleys where water comes off the roof fast. Style selection matters.

name: Fascia and Soffit Repair
title: Fascia & Soffit Repair in DFW | Timber Roofing
description: Fascia and soffit repair for North Texas homes — rot from gutter overflow, damaged soffit panels, and blocked attic intake ventilation.
heroSub: The trim along your roof edge holds the gutters up and lets the attic breathe. Both matter more than it looks.
intro: Fascia is the board along the roof edge that gutters hang from. Soffit is the underside of the overhang, and it is where your attic takes in air. When either fails, the consequences reach further than the appearance of the trim.
Rotted fascia will not hold a gutter. Blocked or damaged soffit starves attic ventilation, which shortens shingle life from underneath.

Water wicking behind the gutter directly onto the fascia.

localNote: Deep eaves are common on North Texas homes built for shade, and those long overhangs mean a lot of fascia and soffit exposed to weather. Combined with the region's heavy rain events, gutter overflow damage along the roof edge is one of the most frequent exterior repairs we see.

faqs.q: Can you replace fascia without removing the gutters?
faqs.a: No. The gutters have to come down to replace what they are hanging from, and they get re-hung afterward.

faqs.q: Does soffit really affect my roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Soffit intake is half of a working ventilation system. Without it, the exhaust vents on your roof cannot move air.

name: Siding Repair

intro: Most North Texas homes are predominantly brick, with siding on gables, dormers, and rear elevations. Those are exactly the areas that take wind-driven rain and hail, and they are frequently the last part of the exterior anyone looks at.
Repairs matter because siding is a water management layer. Cracked panels and open trim joints let moisture behind the cladding, where it does quiet damage to sheathing and framing.

faqs.q: Will repaired siding match?
faqs.a: Rarely perfectly on a weathered wall. We will tell you honestly what to expect before starting rather than after.

faqs.q: Should siding be inspected after hail?
faqs.a: Yes. Gable siding damage is common and frequently missed because everyone is looking at the roof.

faqs.q: Can you paint over failing paint?
faqs.a: Not successfully. Whatever is failing underneath will take the new coating with it. Preparation is where the durability comes from.

faqs.q: When is the best time to paint in Texas?
faqs.a: Avoid the extremes. Surface temperature in mid-summer and cold snaps in winter both cause problems with application and cure.

description: Storm damage repair beyond the roof — gutters, fascia, soffit, siding, and fencing damaged by North Texas hail and wind.
heroSub: Storms do not stop at the roofline, and neither should the inspection.
intro: After a hail or wind event, most attention goes to the roof — reasonably so. But the same storm dents gutters, cracks gable siding, tears soffit panels, and flattens fence sections, and those often get handled months later by a different contractor.
We inspect the exterior as a whole, document what we find, and can address the roof and the rest of it as one project.

signs.d: Soft metal shows hail clearly and is a strong indicator for the roof above.

causes.d: Direct impact on every exposed exterior surface, not just the roof.
Uplift on soffit and roofing, lateral load on fences and gates.
Water into joints and transitions that shed ordinary rain.
Airborne material and falling limbs.

localNote: In a typical Metroplex hail event, the gutters and gable siding often show damage more obviously than the roof does. Those surfaces are useful evidence, and they are also real damage in their own right.

faqs.q: Do you inspect more than the roof after a storm?
faqs.a: Yes. Gutters, fascia, soffit, siding, and fencing are all part of a proper post-storm exterior inspection.

faqs.q: Can exterior damage be handled with the roof work?
faqs.a: Usually, and it is generally simpler that way. The estimate is itemized so you can decide what to do and when.
